s1.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with skin lesions in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: tender annular erythematous plaques on the neck and trunk
abnormal laboratory findings including leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and elevated C-reactive protein
key_facts: recent chemotherapy with ixazomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone
tender lesions on the neck and trunk
annular erythematous plaques with violaceous and crusted centers
skin biopsy showed inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells
immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and myeloperoxidase, negative for CD138

abnormal laboratory findings including leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and elevated C-reactive protein

differentials: Primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma
per_call: Primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Sweet syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: fever, tender skin lesions, and inflammatory infiltrate in an immunocompromised patient

shortlist.label: Ecthyma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: skin lesions with violaceous and crusted centers in a patient with recent chemotherapy and immunocompromised state

shortlist.label: Neutrophilic eccrine hidradenitis
shortlist.why_kept: febrile illness with skin lesions and recent chemotherapy

shortlist.label: Varicella-zoster virus infection
shortlist.why_kept: fever and skin lesions in an immunocompromised patient

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus infection
shortlist.why_kept: febrile illness with skin lesions and immunocompromised state

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of fever, tender lesions, and annular erythematous plaques with violaceous and crusted centers, along with a low white blood cell count and elevated C-reactive protein, is consistent with Sweet syndrome. The skin biopsy findings of an inflammatory infiltrate of predominantly mononuclear cells and immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and myeloperoxidase also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Ecthyma gangrenosum
rejected.why: Typically associated with Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection and not consistent with the patient's negative blood culture and lack of other symptoms

rejected.label: Neutrophilic eccrine hidradenitis
rejected.why: Usually presents with neutrophilic infiltrate and is associated with chemotherapy, but the patient's skin biopsy did not show this

rejected.label: Varicella-zoster virus infection
rejected.why: Typically presents with a vesicular rash and is not consistent with the patient's annular erythematous plaques

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus infection
rejected.why: Not consistent with the patient's clinical presentation and laboratory findings
